newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hails activists' landing, calls for talks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hails activists' landing, calls for talks.

text.p: Taiwan on Monday praised a landing by Hong Kong and Taiwan activists on a group of East China Sea islands but said its dispute with Japan over who controls the chain could be resolved only through negotiations.

"We always admire and recognise acts of patriotism to protect our land," government spokesman Su Chi said on state television. "We also feel very good that they bravely set out to sea and are returning after a rational, peaceful protest."

In the latest challenge to Japan's claim of sovereignty over what it calls the Senkakus, Taiwan and Hong Kong activists landed on one of the unpopulated islets and hoisted the flags of both communist China and Nationalist-ruled Taiwan.
Taiwan and China separately claim the islands, known as the Diaoyus in Chinese.
While lauding the activists' protest sail, Su reiterated Taipei's wish to resolve the row with Japan through dialogue.
"The sovereignty and territorial disputes should all be resolved through negotiations. We will continue to try to resolve the problem through negotations," he said.
Taiwan and Japan have held two rounds of "unofficial" talks over fishing rights near the islands and other issues stemming from the sovereignty row.
Taiwan negotiators said they had failed to reach agreement with their Japanese counterparts in the second round on Friday.
No more talks have been scheduled so far.
Wu Poh-hsiung, secretary-general of Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, also voiced support for Monday's private assertion of Chinese sovereignty over the islands, but cautioned against rash actions.
"As long as people take care of their own safety, we feel it is appropriate for private citizens to deliver some private responses," Wu said.
"But it is vital to avoid a conflict involving military forces," he added.
